materials_mech.principal_stress_3d.title: Principal stresses of a general 3-D stress state

procedure.python:
def _principal_3d(v):
    """Eigenvalues of the symmetric Cauchy stress tensor, sorted σ1 ≥ σ2 ≥ σ3."""
    s = np.array([[v['sx'], v['txy'], v['txz']],
                  [v['txy'], v['sy'], v['tyz']],
                  [v['txz'], v['tyz'], v['sz']]], dtype=float)
    w = np.sort(np.linalg.eigvalsh(s))[::-1]
    s1, s2, s3 = map(float, w)
    vm = math.sqrt(0.5 * ((s1 - s2) ** 2 + (s2 - s3) ** 2 + (s3 - s1) ** 2))
    return {'s1': s1, 's2': s2, 's3': s3, 'tau_abs_max': (s1 - s3) / 2, 'sigma_vm': vm}

method_references: Eigenvalues of the Cauchy stress tensor

assumptions: Plane stress (third principal = 0), proportional loading.

Use von Mises/Tresca for ductile materials (S_y); Coulomb–Mohr/modified Mohr/Rankine for brittle materials (S_ut, S_uc). Coulomb–Mohr with S_yt, S_yc also covers ductile materials with unequal yield strengths.

materials_mech.composite_beam.title: Composite (multi-material) beam by transformed section

variables.name: y_na
variables.desc: neutral axis height above the bottom

procedure.python:
def _composite_beam(v):
    """Transformed-section bending of a stacked rectangular composite beam.

    layers: bottom-to-top [[b (m), h (m), E (Pa)], ...]; M bending moment (N·m, sagging positive, puts the
    top in compression). Each layer is transformed to the reference modulus E_ref by width n·b with
    n = E/E_ref; stress in a layer at height y from the neutral axis is σ = −n M y / I_t.
    """
    layers = v['layers']
    M, Eref = v['M'], v['E_ref']
    y0 = 0.0
    rows = []
    for b, h, E in layers:
        n = E / Eref
        rows.append((n * b, h, y0, n))
        y0 += h
    A = sum(bt * h for bt, h, _, _ in rows)
    ybar = sum(bt * h * (yb + h / 2) for bt, h, yb, _ in rows) / A
    I = sum(bt * h ** 3 / 12 + bt * h * (yb + h / 2 - ybar) ** 2 for bt, h, yb, _ in rows)
    stresses = []
    for (bt, h, yb, n) in rows:
        for y in (yb, yb + h):
            stresses.append([y, -n * M * (y - ybar) / I])
    return {'y_na': ybar, 'I_t': I, 'stress_profile': stresses,
            'sigma_max_abs': max(abs(s) for _, s in stresses)}

assumptions: Perfect bond, plane sections, linear elastic layers of rectangular cross-section.

materials_mech.hertz_spheres.title: Hertzian contact between two spheres

variables.name: d2
variables.desc: diameter of sphere 2 (negative for a concave seat)

assumptions: Elastic, frictionless, smooth, contact small compared to radii. Flat plate: d2 → ∞ (use a very large value). Maximum shear ≈ 0.3 p_max at depth ≈ 0.48a (ν = 0.3).
method_references: Hertz contact of spheres (Shigley eq. form, recalled)

method_references: Hertz contact of cylinders (Shigley eq. form, recalled)

materials_mech.impact_axial.title: Impact from a falling weight on an elastic member
assumptions: Energy conservation, member mass neglected, no rebound losses; h = 0 (suddenly applied) gives factor 2. Stress scales by the same factor: σmax = k_impact σst.
